story.why: It feels like Jack and the Beanstalk, and the pages I saw mostly match the words. Page 2 and page 3 make sense, though the mother/setting look a little artificial and not fully natural.

That said, it is still a stylized cartoon version, so it is not a perfect likeness. On Page 3 the face is a bit more exaggerated and less like the photo, but overall I can tell it is meant to be the same person.

story.why: Yes, it does ring true as Jack and the Beanstalk, and the pictures mostly match the words. Page 2 fits well enough with the old man trading beans for the cow. Page 3 also matches the line about the beans going out the window. Page 1 is a little less clear to me because the wording says they had nothing left to sell but Milky-White, and the scene is crowded and a bit hard to take in at first glance, but it still follows the story.

professional.why: It looks fairly polished and close to something you could buy. The artwork is clean, the colors are nice, and the layout is neat. The text is large and easy to read on all the pages shown. Still, it has that computer-made feeling to it, especially in the faces and in the very smooth, glossy look of the scenes, so I would not call it top store quality.

answer.notGood: The first thing I would change is the very obvious artificial look of the pictures. It does not feel like a real illustrated book yet; it feels generated, and I am skeptical of that sort of thing. Also, the About Me page is odd because it says the child is 22, which does not make sense for what I would expect in a children’s book, and that would make me pause. Page 3 is a little busy, and Page 1 takes a moment to understand because there is a lot happening in the room. I would make the character less generic-looking and make the pages feel a little warmer and more natural.

professional.why: The art is polished in a commercial-AI way, with decent lighting, color design, and consistent scene layout. answer.notGood: Main issue is the AI polish versus actual illustration quality. The face consistency is decent, but the body proportions shift a bit from page to page and the character has that generic 3D/storybook model look. I’d first fix the stiffness in the poses and give Jack more distinctive design language so he feels like a character, not just a face pasted onto a stock child body. Also, the About Me page is very bare-bones and a little too rigid in layout. Page 1 and 3 are the strongest; Page 4 is the least alive.

persona.name: Martin, 58
persona.who: public children's librarian who has read Jack and the Beanstalk aloud hundreds of times
persona.knows: the original tale and its versions
persona.lens: faithfulness to the story: the cow, the beans, the mother, the order of events, the tone

likeness.why: Yes, the child-Jack looks recognizably like the person in the photo, just heavily stylized. The glasses, smile, beard shape, and overall face are there, and the About Me page on page 4 is especially close to the photo. It’s not a literal likeness, but it’s clearly meant to be the same person.

story.why: It does feel like Jack and the Beanstalk in the basic bones of it: the mother, the cow Milky-White, the old man, the magic beans, and the throwing of the beans out the window on page 3. But the sequence is very compressed, and page 2 is a little too cheerful for the moment when Jack trades the cow. The pictures mostly match the words, though the tone is more cute fantasy than the leaner, rougher traditional tale I know.

professional.why: It looks polished and quite finished, especially on pages 1 to 3. The lighting, compositions, and character rendering are strong, and page 4 is laid out cleanly like a product. It still reads as app-made in places, but not cheaply so; it is closer to a store-bought picture book than a homemade one.

answer.notGood: The first thing I would change is the story shaping: it feels a bit too prettified and rushed. Page 2 especially turns a grim bargain into something almost playful, and the emotional stakes of selling the cow are softened. I would also want slightly more consistent character design between the pages, because Jack’s face and proportions shift a little from scene to scene. The About Me page is neat, but for a real picture book I’d rather have more story pages and less of that filler style page.
